on-accent.note: Black on the bundled dark theme and white on the bundled light theme, for 4.5:1 on a solid accent fill.

dim-foreground.source: --sb-muted-fg over --sb-layer-window (55% body colour on the dark tone, 74% on the light tone; 90% on both under prefers-contrast: more)

shadow-ink.note: Shade and shadow tint only; never a text colour.

display.purpose: The one large heading of a first-run, welcome, or placeholder page; never a control label.

title.purpose: Group headings, shell titles, and header bar titles.

body.purpose: Long-form and settings prose, and the titles of rows in boxed lists at regular weight. Line height 1.55 instead of 1.4 for long-form reading.

label.purpose: Compact metadata and state labels; capitalisation follows the Capitalisation Rule. Dimmed 55% on the dark tone, 74% on the light tone.

caption.purpose: Row subtitles and help captions; sentence capitalisation. Shares the size token of Label.

document.purpose: The main content of a view, such as the text of an article or a book. In SillyBunny it is Body at the user's text size; the Body line height applies.

numeric.purpose: Numbers that change or line up in a column: counts, times, progress text, columns of values.

shadows.name: headerbar-shade
shadows.purpose: The line at the edge of a bar. No blurred shadow.

shadows.name: card
shadows.value: 0 0 0 1px <shade 3%>, 0 1px 3px 1px <shade 7%>, 0 2px 6px 2px <shade 3%>; the ring takes the border colour under prefers-contrast: more
shadows.purpose: Card Shadow: a card or group at rest. No separate border.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: Menus, drop-downs, pickers, and search results. The edge is a 1px ring inside the shadow, not a border.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and shell drawers. Paired with one 1px border.

shadows.name: dialog-backdrop
shadows.value: shade colour at about 50% (dark) or 14% (light); no blur

shadows.name: page-transition-shade
shadows.value: covered page: shade colour deepening as it is covered, to about half the dialog backdrop (25% dark, 7% light); sliding page: a soft 56px shadow from its leading edge; only while a page moves
shadows.purpose: Separates a page sliding over another in a page stack. Removed with the slide under reduced motion.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--sb-focus-ring-color), where --sb-focus-ring-color is color-mix(in srgb, var(--sb-focus-ring) 78%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Focus-visible treatment for buttons, tabs, and menu rows; never stacked with an outline or outer ring. Solid-fill buttons (suggested, destructive, send) and controls on a picture (avatars) take focus-ring-outer instead; inside a toast the ring is a light form of the accent, as libadwaita's toast. Fields draw the same colour as their border plus a 1px inset (--sb-entry-focus-border, --sb-entry-focus-ring), which reads as the same 2px ring. About 55% on the dark tone and about 66% on the light tone, above libadwaita's 50%, for 3:1 in both tones. The ring is drawn in Accent, as libadwaita's.

shadows.name: focus-ring-outer
shadows.value: outline: 2px solid var(--sb-focus-ring-color); outline-offset: 1px; box-shadow: none
shadows.purpose: Focus-visible for solid-fill buttons and controls on a picture, where an inset ring does not show.

shadows.name: focus-outline-small
shadows.purpose: Focus-visible for checkboxes and radios, drawn outside with an offset where libadwaita draws inside; ranges use a 4px offset.

shadows.name: drop-target
shadows.value: button: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--sb-accent); other element: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--sb-accent); drop area: inset 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--sb-accent) 40%, transparent) with a color-mix(in srgb, var(--sb-accent) 10%, transparent) fill
shadows.purpose: An element that accepts a drop. No change of fill, except on a whole drop area. Every drag-and-drop action has a keyboard route; Esc cancels a drag.

flatFills.name: flat-hover
flatFills.purpose: Flat button hover, gated behind (hover: hover). A flat button is transparent at rest.

flatFills.name: flat-selected
flatFills.purpose: Selected tab, nav item, or toggled toolbar button.

flatFills.name: raised
flatFills.purpose: Raised controls: a secondary button and the Close circle.

flatFills.name: view-row-selected
flatFills.value: color-mix(in srgb, var(--sb-accent) 25%, transparent); hover 32%; pressed 39%; prefers-contrast: more adds a 1px ring at the border strength

flatFills.name: trough
flatFills.purpose: Range trough and the off trough of a switch.

strengths.name: border
strengths.purpose: Strength of borders and separators, 1px wide. Over the dark Window colour 50% is 4.97:1, above the 3:1 of non-text contrast. Deviation: libadwaita draws a border as the text colour at this strength; SillyBunny draws it in the theme's border colour at the normal contrast, because the border colour is part of the user's theme (The Theme Alias Rule); under prefers-contrast: more it is 50% of the body colour, as libadwaita draws it. Review when libadwaita changes this value.

strengths.name: disabled
strengths.purpose: Disabled controls, labels, status icons and spinners. Lower under high contrast so a disabled control stays distinct from the stronger enabled one.

strengths.name: disabled-nested
strengths.purpose: An icon or label inside a control that is already faded, such as a toggle or the edit icon of an entry row.

strengths.name: quiet-mark
strengths.purpose: Indicators and separators inside menus, and the Caps Lock indicator of a secret field.

strengths.name: trough
strengths.purpose: Progress and scale troughs. The 2px outline of a checkbox or radio uses the trough strength; under prefers-contrast: more it takes the border strength.

strengths.name: window-outline
strengths.purpose: The 1px ring at the edge of a dialog or sheet, inside its shadow.

stateColors.name: link
stateColors.purpose: Links. Pressed returns to this colour; disabled takes the disabled strength. The underline stays so a link never relies on colour alone.

stateColors.name: link-visited
stateColors.purpose: Visited link: Accent mixed 80% with the View ink.

stateColors.name: link-hover
stateColors.value: Accent with its saturation and lightness each multiplied by 1.1
stateColors.purpose: Link on hover: saturation and lightness each multiplied by 1.1.

stateColors.name: link-on-dark-overlay
stateColors.purpose: A link inside a dark overlay such as a tooltip or a toast.

stateColors.name: selection
stateColors.purpose: Selected text. The ink is unchanged.

stateColors.name: selection-focused
stateColors.purpose: Selected text in the field that has focus.

rowPrimitives.name: row
rowPrimitives.value: min-height 50px (taller with a subtitle, as its two lines need); padding 6px 12px; 6px between its parts; the control moves under the title only when the two do not fit; 1px bottom separator, none on the last row of a group
rowPrimitives.purpose: Base settings row: .ds-row-text on the start side, .ds-row-suffix on the end side. The row title is Body at regular weight.

rowPrimitives.name: row-text
rowPrimitives.value: flex 1 1 7em (--sb-row-title-min), so the control moves under it only when both do not fit; min-width 0; wraps

rowPrimitives.name: row-subtitle
rowPrimitives.purpose: Visible description promoted verbatim from title= text; lorum ipsum until final copy.

rowPrimitives.name: row-suffix
rowPrimitives.purpose: Trailing control: select, input, switch, button.

rowPrimitives.name: row-switch
rowPrimitives.value: whole-row label; native checkbox carries role=switch and its checked state; no aria-checked (ARIA in HTML forbids it on input type=checkbox)

rowPrimitives.name: row-check
rowPrimitives.value: whole-row label; native checkbox at the start of the row (a switch stays at the end), no role=switch
rowPrimitives.purpose: Pick-several lists; a one-option boolean uses row-switch.

rowPrimitives.name: row-entry-floating
rowPrimitives.value: linked single-line title inside a filled input; --sb-composer-input-bg, transparent 1px border, the control radius, min-height --sb-field-min-height; focus ring on the input, suffix outside
rowPrimitives.purpose: Single-line entries. Float on focus, value or autofill; the title doubles as the placeholder, and an adopted input's placeholder stays as its accessible description, unpainted. Adopt the input without changing its type.

rowPrimitives.name: row-entry-secret
rowPrimitives.value: placeholder MutationObserver supplies saved/missing icon and visually hidden aria-describedby text; unknown status hidden; -webkit-text-security: disc and Reveal only where supported
rowPrimitives.purpose: API keys without changing the upstream text input type or invoking password-manager behaviour. Deviation: entry, reveal and key management may exceed two controls.

rowPrimitives.name: row-entry-caption
rowPrimitives.value: dimmed Caption below the field, linked by aria-describedby; multi-line instructions remain above; preserve help nodes and gated warnings
rowPrimitives.purpose: Deviation: AdwEntryRow has no subtitle; the floating factory uses its subtitle option as the caption, because it retains upstream help. Review when libadwaita adds a subtitle to entry rows.

rowPrimitives.name: row-toggle
rowPrimitives.value: named radiogroup of label-only native radio segments drawn as a toggle group (see the Toggle Group component); fill stacks the title over equal-width wrapping segments; 44px segments on coarse pointers

rowPrimitives.name: row-select
rowPrimitives.value: hidden adopted native select and adjacent hidden select2 container; trigger shows selected text; whole-row hover, active and inset focus; shared chevron edge
rowPrimitives.purpose: Shared searchable picker mirrors optgroups, disabled options, multiple selection and late loads. Native bubbling change writes back; jQuery change listening follows upstream writes. Ordered multi-selects append new picks. Second trigger/background click closes; opening a competitor closes the current popup.

rowPrimitives.name: row-profile
rowPrimitives.value: select-mirror row with optional summary and suffix spinner; trailing vertical ellipsis only when onMenu exists
rowPrimitives.purpose: Pickers whose items can be grouped or starred; the trailing menu appears only when the row has actions. Folders and favourites follow the native optgroups; actions use existing handlers.

rowPrimitives.name: row-property
rowPrimitives.value: read-only name and value; the name is the subtitle at the Caption size, dimmed; the value is the label at full strength, selectable; Mono role for code or an identifier; no control
rowPrimitives.purpose: Shows a fact the user can read and copy but not change.

rowPrimitives.name: row-spin
rowPrimitives.value: exact number right-aligned at the end with a round minus and plus button, 30px, 6px apart with a fine pointer and 14px with a coarse one (44px targets); the number takes the free width; the row draws the focus ring, not the field
rowPrimitives.purpose: An exact value that matters; otherwise a slider.

rowPrimitives.name: row-button
rowPrimitives.value: 40px inner height; 12px side margin; title in the Title role between optional start and end icons; suggested fills the row with Accent, destructive uses Destructive Red text
rowPrimitives.purpose: An action at the end of a list or part of it, such as adding an item. At most one suggested or destructive button per view.

rowPrimitives.name: row-slider
rowPrimitives.value: range plus 5.5em number field; stacks under the title when the row is too narrow to hold the title, range and number field side by side

rowPrimitives.name: row-expander
rowPrimitives.value: details > summary.ds-row + .ds-row-expander-content; trailing chevron points down when collapsed and up when expanded
rowPrimitives.purpose: Multi-control samplers and other grouped options.

rowPrimitives.name: control-flex
rowPrimitives.purpose: Stable control width regardless of the label length. widthNatural and widthUnset controls keep their natural width.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Hover, press, focus, selection, colour and fill changes.

motion.name: durations
motion.purpose: The durations of the three transitions alone, for a delay or a property whose easing is set elsewhere.

motion.name: spring-dialog
motion.purpose: Alert/Dialog open: scale 0.8 to 1 and fade from centre; clamped 200ms close to scale 0.9. The only pronounced overshoot.

motion.name: spring-sheet
motion.purpose: Window open: scale 0.96 to 1 and fade; Window closes to 0.98. Mobile sheets slide from bottom; shell drawers use fade and scale 0.96 to 1.

motion.name: spring-navigation
motion.purpose: Pushed dialog-page and mobile navigation push/pop, with the page transition shade.

motion.name: popover
motion.value: 200ms fade + scale 0.96 to 1 from the trigger edge; 150ms fade out
motion.purpose: Menus, drop-downs, and result lists. GTK4 popovers do not animate; this is a deliberate origin cue.

motion.name: toast
motion.value: 300ms slide from own height + fade in; 300ms fade + scale to 0.95 out

motion.name: spring-fallback
motion.value: cubic-bezier fallback where CSS linear() is unsupported (Safari < 17.2)
motion.purpose: Springs are sampled into linear() easings.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: no movement or scale; instant or a crossfade of 200ms or less
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion or the Reduced Motion setting. JS helpers are no-ops.

motion.name: side-panel-shift
motion.purpose: The main content shifts when a side panel docks or closes. The panel appears after the content settles.

motion.name: toast-timing
motion.value: 5s on screen; no timeout stays until dismissed; 500ms to replace; paused while hovered, pressed or focused; shows and hides as the toast entry
motion.purpose: A second toast waits behind the first; a high-priority toast shows at once and pushes the first back into the queue. A toast's button runs its action once and is then disabled. Existing toasts move to this timing as the toast layer is rebuilt.

motion.name: spinner
motion.purpose: Spinner turn. A still arc under reduced motion.

motion.name: drag-hover
motion.purpose: A dragged item held over an inactive toggle switches to its view.

breakpoints.name: overlay-sheet
breakpoints.purpose: AdwDialog condition for alerts, dialogs and windows; independent of the 768px shell layout breakpoint.

breakpoints.name: menu-sheet
breakpoints.purpose: Menus and pickers become sheets in the whole mobile layout, so a menu opened there is never a desktop popover.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Shell layout breakpoint: sidebars collapse, List → Split Editor, message action row, mobile-styles.css and coarse layout, and menus and pickers become sheets. Alerts, dialogs and windows use the separate 450px/360px sheet condition.

breakpoints.name: hig-phone-minimum
breakpoints.purpose: Smallest size every layout must support (HIG Scaling & Adaptiveness).

breakpoints.name: hig-desktop-minimum
breakpoints.purpose: Smallest supported desktop size in the HIG.

breakpoints.name: unit
breakpoints.libadwaita: sp (1sp is 1px at regular text size and 1.25px at large text)
breakpoints.purpose: Deviation: libadwaita writes breakpoints in sp, which follows the system's text scale; SillyBunny writes them in px, because a media query cannot read the application's text size setting, so a text-scaled unit would follow only the browser's default size. Review when a media query can read a custom property.

splitViews.name: sidebar-fraction
splitViews.purpose: Default sidebar width. A pattern that gives its own width (a split editor, a side panel) uses that.

splitViews.name: collapse
splitViews.value: navigation split view: a navigation stack with the sidebar as its root page; overlay split view: the sidebar hides and shows over the content on request
splitViews.purpose: The overlaid sidebar uses the Window colour, dims the content with the shade colour and casts a 56px shadow from its edge. Esc hides it while collapsed.

statusPageSets.name: default
statusPageSets.value: icon 128px; title Display; gaps and margins 36px; side margin 12px; text gap 12px

statusPageSets.name: compact
statusPageSets.value: icon 96px; title Headline; gaps and margins 24px
statusPageSets.purpose: Sidebars, popovers, panes; the default for an empty sidebar.

statusPageSets.name: spinner
statusPageSets.value: spinner 64px (stroke 6px, weight 267); title Headline; gaps and margins 24px

radii.name: control
radii.purpose: Controls in bars (destinations, section triggers, Back, actions, fields in a bar), menu rows, search result rows, tooltips, and segments.

radii.name: card
radii.purpose: 12px boxed groups inside editors, dialogs, alerts, windows, and side panels; fill 8% body colour on the dark tone and View on the light tone, with the Card Shadow.

radii.name: overlay
radii.purpose: Popovers, menus, dialogs, shell drawers, and bars that float over content.

radii.name: inner
radii.purpose: A small part inside a control or a row.

radii.name: aliases
radii.value: Control (button, sm, shell control) or Card (md, lg, xl)
radii.purpose: Older names kept for existing rules and user CSS.

radii.name: pill
radii.purpose: A primary text button in open space, circles for Close and an icon-only suggested action, and toasts.

iconSizes.name: normal
iconSizes.purpose: Symbolic icons drawn on a 16px grid; the default size. Deviation: GNOME uses symbolic icons drawn on a 16px grid; SillyBunny uses the Font Awesome glyph set, sized by the text around it, because upstream markup and extensions use that set. Review when the icon set is replaced.

iconSizes.name: large
iconSizes.purpose: An icon that is the focus of attention. HIG sizes are 16, 32, 64 and 128px; others render fuzzy.

iconSizes.name: status-compact
iconSizes.purpose: Icon of the compact status page (sidebar, popover, pane). The one size outside the HIG list: libadwaita's own exception.

iconSizes.name: status-default
iconSizes.purpose: Icon of the default status page.

iconSizes.name: spinner
iconSizes.purpose: Spinner of the loading status page; thinner stroke, 6px at this size.

iconSizes.name: palette
iconSizes.purpose: Colours of status icons. A control shows an icon or a label, not both; sidebars and view switchers are the exception.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: libadwaita suggested action: the single primary confirmation or launch action in a view. A view has at most one suggested or destructive button. Label is an imperative verb in header capitalisation. At least 44px high on coarse pointers. No hover lift.
components.html: <button class="ds-button-primary">Start Writing</button>
components.css: .ds-button-primary { min-height: 38px; padding: 10px 14px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--sb-radius-control); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary, #b1e2ff) 88%, white 12%); color: var(--sb-on-accent, #000); font: 700 14px/1.2 Adwaita Sans, system-ui, Noto Sans, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94); } @media (hover: hover) { .ds-button-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary, #b1e2ff) 82%, white 18%); } } .ds-button-primary:active { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary, #b1e2ff) 82%, white 18%); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--sb-focus-ring-color, color-mix(in srgb, #b1e2ff 55%, transparent)); outline-offset: 1px; box-shadow: none; } @media (pointer: coarse) { .ds-button-primary { min-height: 44px; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-button-primary { transition: none; } }

components.name: Suggested Icon Button
components.description: Icon-only suggested-action circle, such as Send. Disabled, it fades with libadwaita's disabled opacity (50%; 40% under prefers-contrast: more), as any disabled control does. At least 44px on coarse pointers.
components.css: .ds-send { width: 38px; height: 38px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 0; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--color-primary, #b1e2ff); color: var(--sb-on-solid-accent, #000); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94); } .ds-send:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; } @media (prefers-contrast: more) { .ds-send:disabled { opacity: 0.4; } } .ds-send:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--sb-focus-ring-color, color-mix(in srgb, #b1e2ff 55%, transparent)); outline-offset: 1px; box-shadow: none; } @media (pointer: coarse) { .ds-send { width: 44px; height: 44px; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-send { transition: none; } }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Secondary button: a libadwaita raised button, with a 10% body-colour fill at rest, 15% on hover and 30% when pressed. A flat button is transparent at rest and uses the flat fills instead (see Flat Toolbar Button). A button that keeps upstream markup also keeps its upstream 1px theme border. At least 44px high on coarse pointers.
components.html: <button class="ds-button-secondary">Open Panel</button>
components.css: .ds-button-secondary { min-height: 38px; padding: 10px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--SmartThemeBorderColor, #000006); border-radius: var(--sb-radius-control); background: var(--sb-raised-bg, color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 10%, transparent)); color: var(--SmartThemeBodyColor, #ffffff); font: 700 14px/1.2 Adwaita Sans, system-ui, Noto Sans, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94); } @media (hover: hover) { .ds-button-secondary:hover { background: var(--sb-raised-hover-bg, color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 15%, transparent)); } } .ds-button-secondary:active { background: var(--sb-raised-active-bg, color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 30%, transparent)); } .ds-button-secondary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--sb-focus-ring-inset, inset 0 0 0 2px #b1e2ff); } @media (pointer: coarse) { .ds-button-secondary { min-height: 44px; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-button-secondary { transition: none; } }

components.name: Preferences Group
components.description: libadwaita boxed list for settings in the card style: card fill (8% body colour on the dark tone, View on the light tone) and Card Shadow, no separate border, the Card radius (12px), rows at least 50px with 6px 12px padding and 1px separators, 24px between groups, the heading block 6px above the list. Row titles are Body at regular weight; group headings are Title. The bold heading and optional description sit above the list in .ds-pref-group-header, as in AdwPreferencesGroup; headings and row titles use header capitalisation. Group headings carry no icon, as libadwaita's.
components.html:
⚙Notifications

Choose which updates appear
components.css: .ds-pref-group-header { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; margin: 0 0 8px; padding: 0 4px; } .ds-pref-group-heading { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin: 0; padding: 10px 16px 4px; font: 700 var(--sb-type-title, 1em)/1.18 Adwaita Sans, system-ui, Noto Sans, sans-serif; color: var(--sb-shell-text-secondary, #c6c6c7); text-transform: none; letter-spacing: 0; } .ds-pref-group-heading span { color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--SmartThemeBodyColor, #ffffff) 62%, transparent); } .ds-pref-group-subtitle { margin: 0; padding: 0 16px 8px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.4; color: var(--sb-input-placeholder, #c6c6c7); } .ds-pref-group { display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden; border-radius: var(--sb-radius-card); background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--SmartThemeBodyColor, #ffffff) 8%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(0 0 6 / 3%), 0 1px 3px 1px rgb(0 0 6 / 7%), 0 2px 6px 2px rgb(0 0 6 / 3%); color: var(--SmartThemeBodyColor, #ffffff); font-family: Adwaita Sans, system-ui, Noto Sans, sans-serif; } .ds-pref-group > .ds-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 6px; min-height: 50px; padding: 6px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sb-shell-border, #000006); } .ds-pref-group > .ds-row:last-child { border-bottom: 0; } .ds-pref-group .ds-row-text { flex: 1 1 7em; min-width: 0; } .sb-list-editor .ds-pref-group, .sb-editor-sheet .ds-pref-group { border-radius: 12px; } :root[data-sb-surface-tone='light'] .ds-pref-group { background: var(--sb-layer-view, #ffffff); } @media (prefers-contrast: more) { .ds-pref-group { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--SmartThemeBorderColor, #000006), 0 1px 3px 1px rgb(0 0 6 / 7%), 0 2px 6px 2px rgb(0 0 6 / 3%); } }

components.name: Popover List
components.description: Opaque popover for menus, pickers, and search results. A 1px ring inside the popover shadow (not a border), 6px padding for a menu list and 8px for any other popover, flat 9px rows, 32px minimum height (44px on coarse pointers), filled only on hover, press, or keyboard selection. Menus and pickers become sheets in the mobile layout, at max-width 768px or max-height 360px, with a grab handle and a swipe-down that follows the finger; Deviation: GTK popovers stay popovers on mobile; SillyBunny turns menus and pickers into sheets, because a sheet gives 44px rows and reach for the thumb, and the grab handle is the only visible cue that a sheet can be swiped away. Review when libadwaita changes this behaviour. A type-ahead list (the completions or suggestions under a text field) is not a menu: it stays anchored below its field at every size, because the field and the on-screen keyboard must stay in view while the user types.

Aster
Bramble
components.css: .ds-popover { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; padding: 6px; border-radius: 15px; background: var(--sb-layer-popover, #36363a); box-shadow: var(--sb-shadow-popover, 0 0 0 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 5%), 0 1px 5px 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 9%), 0 2px 14px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 5%)); color: var(--SmartThemeBodyColor, #ffffff); font-family: Adwaita Sans, system-ui, Noto Sans, sans-serif; } .ds-popover-row { min-height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; display: flex; align-items: center; border-radius: 9px; cursor: pointer; } @media (hover: hover) { .ds-popover-row:hover { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--SmartThemeBodyColor, #ffffff) 7%, transparent); } } .ds-popover-row:active { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--SmartThemeBodyColor, #ffffff) 16%, transparent); } .ds-popover-row[aria-selected='true'] { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--SmartThemeBodyColor, #ffffff) 10%, transparent); } @media (pointer: coarse) { .ds-popover-row { min-height: 44px; } } @media (prefers-contrast: more) { .ds-popover { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--SmartThemeBorderColor, #000006), 0 1px 5px 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 9%), 0 2px 14px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 5%); } }

components.name: Dialog Tiers
components.description: Alert: Dialog layer, 18px radius, 300px preferred, 372px max (600px wide), one optional boolean, centred heading/body. Dialog: Window layer, forms min(640px, 100% - 32px) wide with a 360px minimum, header and one scrolling body, height follows content up to 90dvh. Window: Window layer, lists/editors/viewers at least 640px and at least as wide as the main content column, never wider than the viewport minus 32px (min(max(640px, var(--sheldWidth)), 100% - 32px)), height follows content up to 90dvh; a fill Window is 90dvh. Explicit action puts Cancel first and affirmative last; immediate apply shows Close. A pushed page shows Back at the start; an immediate-apply page also shows Close, which closes the frame one page at a time and stops at a page that refuses. A page over a sheet keeps the sheet's grab handle; a swipe on it pops the page. An Alert may overlay; nested Dialog/Window is a page. Sheets use max-width 450px or max-height 360px, have a grab handle, and close on a downward swipe. Deviation: libadwaita keeps alert dialogs floating and gives its dialog sheet no grab handle; every overlay here is a bottom sheet with a grab handle, because a sheet gives 44px rows and reach for the thumb, and the grab handle is the only visible cue that a sheet can be swiped away. Review when libadwaita changes this behaviour. Only an Alert stacks its responses full-width.

Resizable sidebar 240–420px, default 30%; collapse at viewport ≤768px or Editor pane <720px. These are defaults; a list inside a Window may set a narrower range and an earlier collapse. Multi-group editors scroll one body, not the shell/detail frame; main text areas have a minimum height and Expand. Explicit-save editors ask Cancel · Discard (destructive) · Save (suggested) before Back, row switches and navigation. The header order is Back, title, dirty indicator, token count, Edit/Preview, item menu, Cancel, Save. On a phone the token count moves to the second row: a single-content editor's toolbar, before its trailing toggles (short form), or beside a list-content editor's property summary. Full list → list shrinks to a sidebar while the editor slides in from the right; reverse on close. SPRING_NAVIGATION (334ms), continuous compression. Clicking another row in the sidebar swaps editor content without replaying the slide, after the dirty check. Reduced motion: instant swap for OS prefers-reduced-motion or body.reduced-motion.

components.name: Banner
components.description: A strip across the top of a view, under its header bar, at the view's full width and outside any scrolling. Hidden until the state it reports applies; revealed with the reveal transition. 6px padding and the Window ink. Its fill is a neutral step over the Window colour. Deviation: libadwaita's banner fill is a fixed grey (#7d7d83) at 30% over the Window colour; SillyBunny mixes the theme's body colour into the Window colour instead, because a fixed colour bypasses user themes (The Theme Alias Rule). Review when libadwaita changes this value. The title is centred or at the start edge, depending on the space; parts are 6px apart, 36px when centred and 9px apart when the button is stacked below the title. The button is at least 84px wide beside the title and 160px wide below it, in the default or the suggested style, and runs the action that resolves the state. Existing banners move to these metrics as each surface is rebuilt.

components.name: Status Page
components.description: Default set: a 128px icon, title in the Display role, 36px between icon and text, 36px above and below and 12px at the sides, 12px between title and description (Body). Compact set, for a sidebar, popover or pane and the default for an empty sidebar: a 96px icon, title in the Headline role, 24px gaps and margins. Spinner set, the loading state: the compact set with the shared spinner (64px, 6px stroke) in place of the icon. The icon is dimmed, fades to the disabled strength when the page is disabled, and uses the heavier stroke (weight 134). The text is clamped to 600px and centred. The page is labelled by its title and described by its description; its icon is hidden from assistive technology. Loading: a view or region that waits for content shows the spinner set in place of the region. The title names what loads, in header capitalisation and without an ellipsis (Loading Documents); a description and an action (Cancel) appear only when they help. It shows only after a short delay (length not yet set), so a quick load shows nothing, and goes when the content is ready. The region is marked aria-busy and the page labels it. A load longer than about 30 seconds, or with a known proportion, shows a progress bar instead. Under reduced motion the spinner stops and shows its still arc.

components.name: Spinner
components.description: Scales between 16px and 64px to the space it is given. Turns once in 1.2 seconds on a track at 15% in the body colour, with a stroke of one eighth of its size (2px at 16px; the status page uses 6px at 64px, weight 267). A label beside it can name the task and add progress as a percentage, time left or items done. Announced as a progress indicator that is busy. Fades to the disabled strength when its control is disabled. Draws a still arc when it is not moving. components.description: The shade ink (#000006) at 80% with white text, a 1px border of white at 10% so it does not melt into a dark background, the Control radius, 6px 10px padding and no shadow; the gap between an icon and text inside it is 6px. Where a control has a visible label, the tooltip adds information or rephrases it and does not repeat it. An icon-only control's tooltip is also its accessible description. narrative.northStar: Simple by default, powerful when needed
narrative.overview:
SillyBunny is an LLM roleplay client that best embodies the HIG (human interface guidelines) of the GNOME project. Although great inspiration is taken from this project, SillyBunny still stands on its own with its own personality and branding based on its focus on roleplay and storywriting. The shell is deliberately kept out of the way so the user can focus on the main content until configuration and navigation are needed.

Intuitive wording, tactile and easily glanceable feedback, and deliberate purpose define the shell. Complex configuration remains available to the user if they wish to seek it (as per upstream SillyTavern), but a good default experience is mandatory and implied - the goal is for a new user to navigate the shell with minimal to no difficulty. Configuration remains behind the shell at all times until called for. All elements of the shell must remain themeable with user CSS themes, and be fully compatible with SillyTavern data, presets, extensions, and settings.

The design philosophies of the GNOME project and its HIG should always be taken into consideration. This means accessibility through lack of distractions, animations that guide the user to what is clicked/tapped, responsive layouts, predictable touch targets, and nothing getting in the way of the main user experience. Mobile design must remain purposefully designed alongside the desktop, adapting libadwaita to a smaller and more touch-heavy window.

With this in mind, SillyBunny can inject its own fun in the design too. After all, it is a roleplay and storywriting client at heart.

This project rejects UI creep, nested menu spirals, configuration sprawl, screen bloat, mystery meat navigation, desktop-only assumptions, and generic SaaS polish.
keyCharacteristics: Content-first main area with no unsolicited permanent configuration panels.
Familiar controls that disclose depth through deliberate input, not visual noise.
Guided animations that promote accessibility and intuitive motion.
Stable desktop and mobile interaction vocabulary, safe shell behaviour for WebKit, Gecko, and Chromium browsers.

rules.name: The Signal Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Accent appears for action, selection, focus, or meaningful state. If removing it does not reduce comprehension, remove it.

rules.name: The Theme Alias Rule
rules.body: New work consumes `SmartTheme*`, `color-*`, `sb-*`, spacing, and radius aliases. Do not hard-code a new color that bypasses saved user themes. `white` and `black` may be mixed into a theme colour with `color-mix()` to lighten or darken it, as libadwaita's stylesheet does; there they are operands, not colours of their own. Deviation: the HIG asks for style variables rather than fixed colours; SillyBunny lets an illustration's backdrop keep its own colour in every theme, because the backdrop belongs to the artwork. It is dropped under forced colours and is never used for anything but the illustration. Review when the HIG changes this advice.

rules.name: The Contrast Rule
rules.body: Body and placeholder text target at least 4.5:1 contrast; large text targets at least 3:1. Muted text can be quiet, but never illegible. Colour is never the only carrier of information; pair it with text, an icon, or shape (HIG UI Styling). Surfaces stay usable under `prefers-contrast: more` and `forced-colors: active`.

rules.name: The Opaque Shell Rule
rules.body: Header bars, drawers, popovers, menus, dialogs, and toasts are opaque. No `backdrop-filter` on shell layers; background images may show only through the canvas and the content surface at the theme's own tint alpha. Tooltips and overlaid controls are the two translucent exceptions.

rules.name: The Single Shell Rule
rules.body: The shell has one libadwaita direction; UI themes, custom CSS, and the accent colour are the theming surface.

rules.name: The Interface Sans Rule
rules.body: Use the interface stack for controls, tabs, labels, and dense settings. Decorative type must never make repeated work harder.

rules.name: The User Scale Rule
rules.body: Product type follows `--mainFontSize` and existing user preferences. Do not add viewport-driven type or a parallel density system.

rules.name: The Wrap Safety Rule
rules.body: Headings use balanced wrapping where supported, and all labels must tolerate long translations, zoom, and narrow mobile widths without overflow.

rules.name: The Capitalisation Rule
rules.body: Follow the HIG Writing Style. Header capitalisation for headings (group, list, page, sheet, and dialog titles), header bar and view titles, view switcher and tab labels, button labels, menu items, tooltips, field labels, and boxed-list row titles; capitalise the first and last word, nouns, verbs, hyphenated words, and every word of four or more letters. Sentence capitalisation for checkbox and radio labels, drop-down items, placeholders, row subtitles, captions, and body text. Headings omit articles and auxiliary verbs; an informal heading written as a full sentence uses sentence capitalisation and stays bold. Never all caps or uppercase tracked kickers. Group headings are bold and carry no icon, as libadwaita's group titles. Deviation: the HIG Writing Style, Drop-Down Lists and Spin Buttons pages ask for sentence capitalisation on field, drop-down and spin-button labels, while the Text Fields and Switches pages ask for header capitalisation; SillyBunny uses header capitalisation for every field label and boxed-list row title, because a group then reads consistently. Review when the HIG resolves this conflict. Upstream SillyTavern strings keep their wording and data-i18n keys; existing sentence-case labels move to this rule as each surface is reworked.

rules.name: The Layer Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Establish a tonal surface before adding elevation. If a shadow is doing all the work, the surface token is wrong.

rules.name: The Flat Toolbar Rule
rules.body: Toolbar and navigation buttons are transparent at rest. Hover, press, and selection use neutral fills mixed from the body color, with no borders, bottom stripes, underlines, glows, or hover lift. Hover fills apply only under `(hover: hover)`.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` or the Reduced Motion setting removes movement and scale. State changes become instant or a crossfade of 200ms or less. JS helpers are no-ops under reduced motion.

rules.name: The WebKit Reliability Rule
rules.body: Prefer solid surfaces on mobile. Fixed layers must respect safe areas, keyboard resizing, scrolling, and focus behavior in Safari/WebKit.

rules.name: The Layer Order Rule
rules.body: Layers stack in this order, lowest to highest: dropdown, sticky, shell, overlay, modal, toast. A new layer takes the place of the kind it is and never sits above a toast.

rules.name: The State-Only Motion Rule
rules.body: Animate state, origin, and destination only. No decorative choreography, ambient loops, or hover lift. Only the dialog spring has a pronounced overshoot. A loading indicator or a spinner shows the busy state and may move in place while it lasts. Deviation: the HIG animates to show state, origin, and destination; SillyBunny also lets an illustration move in place, because the art is content, not interface motion. Review when the HIG changes this rule. Such motion stays inside the illustration, the indicator or the spinner, never moves layout, pauses while it is hidden, and stops under the Reduced Motion Rule, which shows the first frame (a loading indicator shows finished; a spinner shows its still arc).

dos: Do keep main content uninterrupted and let configuration appear only after deliberate input.
Do give every view at most one suggested or destructive button, then place powerful options behind learnable progressive disclosure.
Do preserve SillyTavern-compatible settings, character data, chats, presets, extensions, and migration paths.
Do use `SmartTheme*`, `sb-*`, `color-*`, spacing, and radius tokens so user themes continue to work.
Do keep desktop and mobile gestures, ordering, labels, and action vocabulary consistent.
Do provide visible focus, semantic labels, comfortable touch targets, resilient wrapping, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do use tonal surfaces before shadows and verify text contrast before shipping.

Do make every action possible with the keyboard as well as with a pointer or touch. Custom shortcuts use Ctrl with a letter, never Alt (reserved for access keys) or Super. Support the standard navigation keys on custom controls: Tab and Shift+Tab move focus, Ctrl+Tab moves it where Tab has another function (a text field), Return activates, Space toggles, F10 opens the primary or secondary menu, Menu or Shift+F10 opens the context menu for the focused item, and arrow keys move around a group of related controls. A control's label immediately precedes it in the focus order. Esc closes popovers, sheets, and dialogs (HIG Keyboard, Popovers, Windows).

Do test every surface with a high-contrast or forced-colours mode, 200% text size, the keyboard alone, a screen reader, and an on-screen keyboard (HIG Accessibility). Every element has a short, descriptive accessible name.

Do write UI text by the HIG Writing Style: short and neutral, familiar terms over system terms, "your" over "my" when ownership must be stated, no Latin abbreviations ("for example", not "e.g."), and no trailing period on labels, headings, or descriptions. An ellipsis (`…`, U+2026) ends a label only when more input or confirmation follows ("Delete…", not "Preferences…"). Never build one sentence from several strings or controls, so translations stay intact. Use typographic characters: “quotes”, ’ apostrophes, – ranges, × dimensions, a bullet `•` (U+2022) in an inline list, and a narrow no-break space (U+202F) between a number and its unit ("32 GB") (HIG Typography).

Do translate each new counter or sentence as one string with placeholders, never joined fragments. Use `…`, never three periods, in new labels. Reuse existing upstream strings and keys verbatim, including trailing periods; the punctuation rule applies to new copy. Unsupplied descriptions, help, and dialog bodies use exactly `TODO(copy)`, marked with `data-sb-copy-placeholder="true"` and reported for maintainer replacement; do not draft project prose.
donts: Don't add configuration panels, extra toolbars, or utility panes to the main content view unless the user opens them. Navigation sidebars, split views, and utility panes follow the HIG (Navigation): each view keeps one clear subject, and panes collapse or overlay at narrow widths.
Don't create a nested menu spiral: no nested submenus, and hierarchies generally one level deep below a view (HIG Menus, Navigation).
Don't present configuration sprawl, bottom bar bloat, or a dense control wall by default.
Don't interrupt the user's main task with a modal for non-critical configuration; try inline or progressive alternatives first.
Don't rely on mystery meat navigation, hover-only discovery, desktop-only assumptions, tiny touch targets, or fragile iOS WebKit behavior.
Don't use generic SaaS polish, sterile upstream-clone blandness, or decorative motion without navigational purpose, except an illustration moving in place (Motion).
Don't use gradient text, decorative glassmorphism, backdrop blur on shell layers, ambient accent glows, repeating stripe or grid backgrounds, identical repeated card grids, or sketchy illustrations.
Don't use `border-left` or `border-right` greater than `1px` as a colored accent.
Don't pair a `1px` border with a shadow of `16px` blur or more on a resting surface. Overlays may keep one border and one overlay shadow.
Don't use uppercase tracked kickers for group or list headings, or hover lift on buttons.
Don't rely on tooltips, hover, or colour alone to carry essential information.
Don't use radii above `20px` for cards or sections, or let long labels and headings overflow narrow viewports.
Don't introduce new pure black or pure white surfaces, or silently overwrite compatible user configuration.
